tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。

6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

198	/// MLA decode forward for one token (bs=1): runs the projections, assembles the
199	/// FlashMLA query, writes the new token into the paged cache at `position`,
200	/// attends over the cached context, and projects back to `o[6144]`.
201	///
202	/// Allocating convenience over the `_into` halves for the oracle-gate/test
203	/// paths (per-call scratch). `cache` is the fp8_ds_mla paged cache (656
204	/// bytes/token); `cos`/`sin` are the position's rotary table first half
205	/// (`[32]`); `topk` is the (fixed-2048, -1-padded) sparse index list; `sched`
206	/// carries the FlashMLA launch sizing (its contract) plus the precomputed
207	/// tile-scheduler plan.
208	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
209	#[cfg(test)]
210	pub(crate) fn glm52_mla_decode_forward(
211	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
212	    w: &Glm52MlaLayerWeights,
213	    hidden: &Rows<HIDDEN>,
214	    cos: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
215	    sin: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
216	    cache: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
217	    position: usize,
218	    topk: &CudaSlice<i32>,
219	    sched: &Glm52MlaSchedMetadata,
220	) -> Result<Rows<HIDDEN>> {
221	    ensure!(
222	        position < sched.contract.num_blocks * GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PAGE_SIZE,
223	        "GLM5.2 MLA position {position} outside paged cache ({} blocks x {GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PAGE_SIZE})",
224	        sched.contract.num_blocks
225	    );
226	    // Front, attend scratch, and output all sized from the plan's contract —
227	    // the same one-construction-point coherence the production bucket state
228	    // provides.
229	    let mut front = Glm52MlaFront::new(ctx, sched.batch(), w.heads)?;
230	    let mut attend = Glm52MlaAttendScratch::new(ctx, &sched.contract, w.heads)?;
231	    let mut slot_mapping = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<i64>(1)?;
232	    let seq_lens = ctx.stream.clone_htod(&[(position + 1) as i32])?;
233	    ctx.stream
234	        .memcpy_htod(&[position as i64], &mut slot_mapping)?;
235	    let mut o = Rows::zeros(ctx, sched.batch())?;
236	    glm52_mla_front_into(ctx, w, hidden, &mut front, sched.folds_kv_pack())?;
237	    glm52_mla_attend_into(
238	        ctx,
239	        w,
240	        &front,
241	        cos,
242	        sin,
243	        cache,
244	        0,
245	        &slot_mapping,
246	        topk,
247	        &seq_lens,
248	        sched,
249	        &mut attend,
250	        &mut o,
251	    )?;
252	    Ok(o)
253	}

255	/// A FlashMLA sparse decode contract paired with its tile-scheduler plan. The
256	/// plan depends only on `batch_size`, `topk` and `num_sm_parts` — not on
257	/// position, sequence length, or layer — so it is computed once (model build
258	/// time) instead of per layer per step (78 × ~25 µs/step at bs=1). Owning the
259	/// contract makes a plan/contract mismatch unrepresentable: every consumer
260	/// reads both from the same object.
261	pub(crate) struct Glm52MlaSchedMetadata {
262	    contract: Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
263	    backend: Glm52MlaBackendSchedule,
264	}
265	
266	enum Glm52MlaBackendSchedule {
267	    FlashMla {
268	        tile_scheduler_metadata: CudaSlice<i32>,
269	        num_splits: CudaSlice<i32>,
270	    },
271	    FlashInfer,
272	}
273	
274	impl Glm52MlaSchedMetadata {
275	    #[cfg(test)]
276	    pub(crate) fn new(
277	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
278	        contract: Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
279	        heads: usize,
280	    ) -> Result<Self> {
281	        Self::new_for_backend(ctx, contract, heads, Glm52MlaBackend::FlashMlaFp8Ds)
282	    }
283	
284	    pub(crate) fn new_for_backend(
285	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
286	        contract: Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
287	        _heads: usize,
288	        backend: Glm52MlaBackend,
289	    ) -> Result<Self> {
290	        let backend = match backend {
291	            Glm52MlaBackend::FlashMlaFp8Ds => {
292	                let mut tile_scheduler_metadata = ctx
293	                    .stream
294	                    .alloc_zeros::<i32>(contract.tile_scheduler_metadata_len())?;
295	                let mut num_splits = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<i32>(contract.num_splits_len())?;
296	                glm52_flashmla_sparse_decode_metadata_launch(
297	                    ctx,
298	                    contract.batch_size,
299	                    contract.topk,
300	                    contract.num_sm_parts,
301	                    &mut tile_scheduler_metadata,
302	                    &mut num_splits,
303	                )?;
304	                Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashMla {
305	                    tile_scheduler_metadata,
306	                    num_splits,
307	                }
308	            }
309	            Glm52MlaBackend::FlashInferFp8 => Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashInfer,
310	        };
311	        Ok(Self { contract, backend })
312	    }
313	
314	    /// Rebind the plan to the launch-decided pool block count. The tile
315	    /// scheduler plan depends only on `batch_size`/`topk`/`num_sm_parts`, so
316	    /// the plan built before the measured KV fill stays valid — only the
317	    /// cache-geometry field the attend launches read needs the real count.
318	    pub(crate) fn set_num_blocks(&mut self, num_blocks: usize) {
319	        self.contract.num_blocks = num_blocks;
320	    }
321	
322	    /// The sparse index-list length this plan was built for. The DSA indexer
323	    /// must produce its top-k with the same k — reading it from the plan makes
324	    /// an indexer/attend mismatch unrepresentable.
325	    pub(crate) fn topk(&self) -> usize {
326	        self.contract.topk
327	    }
328	
329	    /// The decode row count this plan was built for — the single source of
330	    /// truth for a step's batch shape (every consumer reads it from here).
331	    pub(crate) fn batch(&self) -> usize {
332	        self.contract.batch_size
333	    }
334	
335	    /// Whether the attend half packs the cache with the fused front kernel
336	    /// (query assemble + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack in one launch): the MLA
337	    /// front must then leave `front.ckv` raw and skip the split/norm.
338	    pub(crate) fn folds_kv_pack(&self) -> bool {
339	        matches!(self.backend, Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashInfer)
340	    }
341	}

343	/// MLA attend half over the plan's `batch()` rows: consumes the front
344	/// projections + the per-row sparse top-k, packs each row's new token into
345	/// its paged-cache slot, runs FlashMLA sparse decode, and projects back into
346	/// `out[T, 6144]`. Every intermediate lives in the persistent attend scratch
347	/// — the chain is allocation-free. `cos`/`sin` carry one `[32]` row per token
348	/// (each row sits at its own position); `slot_mapping`/`topk` are `[T]` /
349	/// `[T, topk]`. `kv_layer_offset` is this layer's MLA slice offset inside
350	/// `cache` (0 for a dedicated arena); it rides each call because one plan
351	/// serves every layer, and the plan's contract carries the block stride.
352	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
353	pub(crate) fn glm52_mla_attend_into(
354	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
355	    w: &Glm52MlaLayerWeights,
356	    front: &Glm52MlaFront,
357	    cos: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
358	    sin: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
359	    cache: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
360	    kv_layer_offset: usize,
361	    slot_mapping: &CudaSlice<i64>,
362	    topk: &CudaSlice<i32>,
363	    seq_lens: &CudaSlice<i32>,
364	    sched: &Glm52MlaSchedMetadata,
365	    s: &mut Glm52MlaAttendScratch,
366	    out: &mut Rows<HIDDEN>,
367	) -> Result<()> {
368	    let contract = Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode {
369	        kv_layer_offset_bytes: kv_layer_offset,
370	        ..sched.contract
371	    };
372	    let t = contract.batch_size;
373	    ensure!(
374	        w.heads == front.heads && w.heads == s.heads,
375	        "GLM5.2 MLA attend head mismatch: weights {}, front {}, scratch {}",
376	        w.heads,
377	        front.heads,
378	        s.heads
379	    );
380	    let heads = w.heads;
381	    // Each row's new token is written to cache slot `slot_mapping[row]`
382	    // (device data, so the launch replays under CUDA graph capture); the
383	    // cache-pack kernel traps on a slot outside the paged window. The
384	    // every-step host guard is the caller's position bound (`decode_step`
385	    // prologue: position < max_model_len and each row confined to its
386	    // own slot region by construction).
387	
388	    // ---- absorb: ql_nope[T,heads,512] = q_pass @ W_UK ----
389	    // cuBLAS batches over this instance's heads (the full 64 or an
390	    // attention-TP shard); the T rows ride the GEMM's n dimension — column t
391	    // of head h reads q_full[t, h, 0..192] (ldb = the compact [T,heads,256]
392	    // token stride) and writes ql_nope[t, h, 0..512] (ldc = the compact
393	    // [T,heads,512] token stride).
394	    gemm_strided_batched_bf16(
395	        ctx,
396	        false,
397	        false,
398	        KV_LORA,
399	        t,
400	        QK_NOPE,
401	        &w.w_uk,
402	        KV_LORA,
403	        QK_NOPE * KV_LORA,
404	        &front.q_full,
405	        heads * Q_HEAD,
406	        Q_HEAD,
407	        &mut s.ql_nope,
408	        heads * KV_LORA,
409	        KV_LORA,
410	        heads,
411	    )?;
412	
413	    let (latent, latent_token_stride) = match (&sched.backend, &mut s.backend) {
414	        (
415	            schedule @ Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashMla { .. },
416	            Glm52MlaBackendScratch::Fp8Ds(scratch),
417	        ) => {
418	            glm52_mla_query_assemble_launch(
419	                ctx,
420	                t,
421	                heads,
422	                &s.ql_nope,
423	                &front.q_full,
424	                QK_NOPE,
425	                Q_HEAD,
426	                cos,
427	                sin,
428	                &mut scratch.query,
429	            )?;
430	            // UE8M0 scales: the FlashMLA fp8_ds_mla cache contract — the sm100
431	            // kernel truncates stored scales to powers of two (see the quant
432	            // kernel's comment); amax/448 scales silently lose up to 1 bit of
433	            // V/K magnitude per group on GB300.
434	            glm52_fp8_per_token_group_quant_bf16_ue8m0_launch(
435	                ctx,
436	                Glm52MoeQuantShape {
437	                    rows: t,
438	                    width: KV_LORA,
439	                    group_size: FP8_BLOCK,
440	                },
441	                &front.kv_c,
442	                &mut scratch.ckv_fp8,
443	                &mut scratch.ckv_scales,
444	            )?;
445	            glm52_mla_cache_pack_launch(
446	                ctx,
447	                t,
448	                &scratch.ckv_fp8,
449	                &scratch.ckv_scales,
450	                &front.k_pe,
451	                cos,
452	                sin,
453	                cache,
454	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes,
455	                contract.kv_block_stride_bytes,
456	                contract.num_blocks,
457	                slot_mapping,
458	            )?;
459	            match (schedule, &mut scratch.attend) {
460	                (
461	                    Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashMla {
462	                        tile_scheduler_metadata,
463	                        num_splits,
464	                    },
465	                    Glm52Fp8DsAttendScratch::FlashMla {
466	                        lse,
467	                        lse_accum,
468	                        o_accum,
469	                    },
470	                ) => glm52_flashmla_sparse_decode_launch(
471	                    ctx,
472	                    contract,
473	                    &scratch.query,
474	                    cache,
475	                    topk,
476	                    tile_scheduler_metadata,
477	                    num_splits,
478	                    &mut scratch.latent,
479	                    lse,
480	                    lse_accum,
481	                    o_accum,
482	                )?,
483	                _ => anyhow::bail!("GLM5.2 FP8-DS MLA schedule/scratch backend mismatch"),
484	            }
485	            (&scratch.latent, HEADS * KV_LORA)
486	        }
487	        (Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashInfer, Glm52MlaBackendScratch::FlashInfer(scratch)) => {
488	            // The FlashInfer pack/attend launches address the cache dense
489	            // from its base — this backend's cache never rides a strided
490	            // slab layout.
491	            ensure!(
492	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes == 0,
493	                "GLM5.2 FlashInfer sparse decode requires a dense cache (layer offset {})",
494	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes
495	            );
496	            // One fused launch: query assemble + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack
497	            // (the split/norm were skipped in `glm52_mla_front_rest_into` for
498	            // this backend — the raw kv_a output is consumed directly).
499	            glm52_mla_front_pack_fp8_launch(
500	                ctx,
501	                t,
502	                heads,
503	                &s.ql_nope,
504	                &front.q_full,
505	                QK_NOPE,
506	                Q_HEAD,
507	                &front.ckv,
508	                &w.kv_a_ln.data,
509	                RMS_EPS,
510	                cos,
511	                sin,
512	                &mut scratch.query,
513	                cache,
514	                slot_mapping,
515	            )?;
516	            glm52_flashinfer_sparse_mla_fp8_launch(
517	                ctx,
518	                Glm52FlashInferSparseDecode {
519	                    batch_size: t,
520	                    heads,
521	                    num_blocks: contract.num_blocks,
522	                    topk: contract.topk,
523	                    sm_scale: contract.sm_scale,
524	                },
525	                &scratch.query,
526	                cache,
527	                topk,
528	                seq_lens,
529	                &mut scratch.latent,
530	                &mut scratch.workspace,
531	            )?;
532	            (&scratch.latent, heads * KV_LORA)
533	        }
534	        _ => anyhow::bail!("GLM5.2 MLA schedule/scratch backend mismatch"),
535	    };
536	
537	    // ---- back: v[T,heads,256] = latent @ W_UV, then o_proj ----
538	    // latent stays full-width [T,64,512] (FlashMLA output); the batch count
539	    // reads only the shard's head slots. v is compact — exactly the sliced
540	    // o_proj's k = heads * 256 input.
541	    gemm_strided_batched_bf16(
542	        ctx,
543	        true,
544	        false,
545	        V_HEAD,
546	        t,
547	        KV_LORA,
548	        &w.w_uv,
549	        KV_LORA,
550	        V_HEAD * KV_LORA,
551	        latent,
552	        latent_token_stride,
553	        KV_LORA,
554	        &mut s.v,
555	        heads * V_HEAD,
556	        V_HEAD,
557	        heads,
558	    )?;
559	    if let Some(wide) = s.wide.as_mut() {
560	        return crate::fp8::fp8_linear_large_m_into(ctx, &w.o_proj, t, &s.v, wide, out.data_mut());
561	    }
562	    fp8_linear_into(
563	        ctx,
564	        &w.o_proj,
565	        t,
566	        &s.v,
567	        Some(&mut s.gemv_partial),
568	        out.data_mut(),
569	    ) // [T, 6144]
570	}

3	//!
4	//! Composes the oracle-validated GPU ops into one callable forward — the
5	//! attention half of a decode layer. The pieces are each gated against the HF
6	//! MLA oracle in `tests/mla_decode_oracle.rs` (front projections, the rope/query/
7	//! cache-pack assembly, FlashMLA sparse decode, the back-half v_up/o_proj); this
8	//! module wires them with no new math.
9	//!
10	//! Weights are taken as raw fp8 bytes (`from_host`) and uploaded once — the module
11	//! is loader-agnostic (functional core). kv_b is pre-dequantized into the bf16
12	//! absorb factors W_UK / W_UV at construction; the fp8 projection weights stay
13	//! as-loaded and every projection relays its activation scale into the TRTLLM
14	//! col-major TMA layout before the blockscale linear (the documented footgun).

135	impl Glm52MlaAttendScratch {
136	    #[cfg(test)]
137	    fn new(
138	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
139	        contract: &Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
140	        heads: usize,

145	    pub(crate) fn new_for_backend(
146	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
147	        contract: &Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
148	        heads: usize,
149	        backend: Glm52MlaBackend,
150	    ) -> Result<Self> {
151	        ensure!(
152	            (1..=HEADS).contains(&heads),
153	            "GLM5.2 MLA attend heads {heads} out of 1..={HEADS}"
154	        );
155	        let t = contract.batch_size;
156	        let backend = match backend {
157	            Glm52MlaBackend::FlashMlaFp8Ds => {
158	                Glm52MlaBackendScratch::Fp8Ds(Box::new(Glm52Fp8DsScratch {
159	                    query: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(t * HEADS * QUERY_DIM)?,
160	                    latent: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(contract.latent_len())?,
161	                    attend: Glm52Fp8DsAttendScratch::FlashMla {
162	                        lse: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<f32>(contract.lse_len())?,
163	                        lse_accum: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<f32>(contract.lse_accum_len())?,
164	                        o_accum: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<f32>(contract.o_accum_len())?,
165	                    },
166	                    ckv_fp8: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(t * KV_LORA)?,
167	                    ckv_scales: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<f32>(t * (KV_LORA / FP8_BLOCK))?,
168	                }))
169	            }
170	            Glm52MlaBackend::FlashInferFp8 => {
171	                Glm52MlaBackendScratch::FlashInfer(Box::new(Glm52FlashInferScratch {
172	                    query: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(t * heads * QUERY_DIM)?,
173	                    latent: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(t * heads * KV_LORA)?,
174	                    workspace: ctx
175	                        .stream
176	                        .alloc_zeros::<u8>(GLM52_FLASHINFER_SPARSE_WORKSPACE_BYTES)?,
177	                }))
178	            }
179	        };
180	        Ok(Self {
181	            ql_nope: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(t * heads * KV_LORA)?,
182	            v: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(t * heads * V_HEAD)?,
183	            backend,
184	            heads,
185	            gemv_partial: ctx
186	                .stream
187	                .alloc_zeros::<f32>(t * GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW)?,
188	            wide: (t > crate::fp8::FP8_GEMV_MAX_ROWS)
189	                .then(|| {
190	                    // o_proj consumes the [T, heads * V_HEAD] attention out.
191	                    crate::fp8::Glm52Fp8GemmScratch::new(ctx, t.next_multiple_of(4), heads * V_HEAD)
192	                })
193	                .transpose()?,
194	        })
195	    }
196	}

198	/// MLA decode forward for one token (bs=1): runs the projections, assembles the
199	/// FlashMLA query, writes the new token into the paged cache at `position`,
200	/// attends over the cached context, and projects back to `o[6144]`.
201	///
202	/// Allocating convenience over the `_into` halves for the oracle-gate/test
203	/// paths (per-call scratch). `cache` is the fp8_ds_mla paged cache (656
204	/// bytes/token); `cos`/`sin` are the position's rotary table first half
205	/// (`[32]`); `topk` is the (fixed-2048, -1-padded) sparse index list; `sched`
206	/// carries the FlashMLA launch sizing (its contract) plus the precomputed
207	/// tile-scheduler plan.
208	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
209	#[cfg(test)]
210	pub(crate) fn glm52_mla_decode_forward(
211	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
212	    w: &Glm52MlaLayerWeights,
213	    hidden: &Rows<HIDDEN>,
214	    cos: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
215	    sin: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
216	    cache: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
217	    position: usize,
218	    topk: &CudaSlice<i32>,
219	    sched: &Glm52MlaSchedMetadata,
220	) -> Result<Rows<HIDDEN>> {
221	    ensure!(
222	        position < sched.contract.num_blocks * GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PAGE_SIZE,
223	        "GLM5.2 MLA position {position} outside paged cache ({} blocks x {GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PAGE_SIZE})",
224	        sched.contract.num_blocks
225	    );
226	    // Front, attend scratch, and output all sized from the plan's contract —
227	    // the same one-construction-point coherence the production bucket state
228	    // provides.
229	    let mut front = Glm52MlaFront::new(ctx, sched.batch(), w.heads)?;
230	    let mut attend = Glm52MlaAttendScratch::new(ctx, &sched.contract, w.heads)?;
231	    let mut slot_mapping = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<i64>(1)?;
232	    let seq_lens = ctx.stream.clone_htod(&[(position + 1) as i32])?;
233	    ctx.stream
234	        .memcpy_htod(&[position as i64], &mut slot_mapping)?;
235	    let mut o = Rows::zeros(ctx, sched.batch())?;
236	    glm52_mla_front_into(ctx, w, hidden, &mut front, sched.folds_kv_pack())?;
237	    glm52_mla_attend_into(
238	        ctx,
239	        w,
240	        &front,
241	        cos,
242	        sin,
243	        cache,
244	        0,
245	        &slot_mapping,
246	        topk,
247	        &seq_lens,
248	        sched,
249	        &mut attend,
250	        &mut o,
251	    )?;
252	    Ok(o)
253	}

255	/// A FlashMLA sparse decode contract paired with its tile-scheduler plan. The
256	/// plan depends only on `batch_size`, `topk` and `num_sm_parts` — not on
257	/// position, sequence length, or layer — so it is computed once (model build
258	/// time) instead of per layer per step (78 × ~25 µs/step at bs=1). Owning the
259	/// contract makes a plan/contract mismatch unrepresentable: every consumer
260	/// reads both from the same object.
261	pub(crate) struct Glm52MlaSchedMetadata {
262	    contract: Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
263	    backend: Glm52MlaBackendSchedule,
264	}

267	    FlashMla {
268	        tile_scheduler_metadata: CudaSlice<i32>,
269	        num_splits: CudaSlice<i32>,
270	    },
271	    FlashInfer,
272	}

274	impl Glm52MlaSchedMetadata {

286	        contract: Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode,
287	        _heads: usize,
288	        backend: Glm52MlaBackend,
289	    ) -> Result<Self> {
290	        let backend = match backend {
291	            Glm52MlaBackend::FlashMlaFp8Ds => {
292	                let mut tile_scheduler_metadata = ctx
293	                    .stream
294	                    .alloc_zeros::<i32>(contract.tile_scheduler_metadata_len())?;
295	                let mut num_splits = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<i32>(contract.num_splits_len())?;
296	                glm52_flashmla_sparse_decode_metadata_launch(
297	                    ctx,

299	                    contract.topk,
300	                    contract.num_sm_parts,
301	                    &mut tile_scheduler_metadata,
302	                    &mut num_splits,
303	                )?;

305	                    tile_scheduler_metadata,

307	                }

314	    /// Rebind the plan to the launch-decided pool block count. The tile
315	    /// scheduler plan depends only on `batch_size`/`topk`/`num_sm_parts`, so
316	    /// the plan built before the measured KV fill stays valid — only the
317	    /// cache-geometry field the attend launches read needs the real count.
318	    pub(crate) fn set_num_blocks(&mut self, num_blocks: usize) {
319	        self.contract.num_blocks = num_blocks;
320	    }

322	    /// The sparse index-list length this plan was built for. The DSA indexer
323	    /// must produce its top-k with the same k — reading it from the plan makes
324	    /// an indexer/attend mismatch unrepresentable.
325	    pub(crate) fn topk(&self) -> usize {
326	        self.contract.topk
327	    }
328	
329	    /// The decode row count this plan was built for — the single source of
330	    /// truth for a step's batch shape (every consumer reads it from here).
331	    pub(crate) fn batch(&self) -> usize {
332	        self.contract.batch_size
333	    }
334	
335	    /// Whether the attend half packs the cache with the fused front kernel
336	    /// (query assemble + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack in one launch): the MLA
337	    /// front must then leave `front.ckv` raw and skip the split/norm.
338	    pub(crate) fn folds_kv_pack(&self) -> bool {
339	        matches!(self.backend, Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashInfer)

343	/// MLA attend half over the plan's `batch()` rows: consumes the front
344	/// projections + the per-row sparse top-k, packs each row's new token into
345	/// its paged-cache slot, runs FlashMLA sparse decode, and projects back into
346	/// `out[T, 6144]`. Every intermediate lives in the persistent attend scratch
347	/// — the chain is allocation-free. `cos`/`sin` carry one `[32]` row per token
348	/// (each row sits at its own position); `slot_mapping`/`topk` are `[T]` /
349	/// `[T, topk]`. `kv_layer_offset` is this layer's MLA slice offset inside
350	/// `cache` (0 for a dedicated arena); it rides each call because one plan
351	/// serves every layer, and the plan's contract carries the block stride.
352	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
353	pub(crate) fn glm52_mla_attend_into(
354	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
355	    w: &Glm52MlaLayerWeights,
356	    front: &Glm52MlaFront,
357	    cos: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
358	    sin: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
359	    cache: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
360	    kv_layer_offset: usize,
361	    slot_mapping: &CudaSlice<i64>,
362	    topk: &CudaSlice<i32>,
363	    seq_lens: &CudaSlice<i32>,
364	    sched: &Glm52MlaSchedMetadata,
365	    s: &mut Glm52MlaAttendScratch,
366	    out: &mut Rows<HIDDEN>,
367	) -> Result<()> {
368	    let contract = Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode {
369	        kv_layer_offset_bytes: kv_layer_offset,
370	        ..sched.contract
371	    };
372	    let t = contract.batch_size;
373	    ensure!(
374	        w.heads == front.heads && w.heads == s.heads,
375	        "GLM5.2 MLA attend head mismatch: weights {}, front {}, scratch {}",
376	        w.heads,
377	        front.heads,
378	        s.heads
379	    );
380	    let heads = w.heads;
381	    // Each row's new token is written to cache slot `slot_mapping[row]`
382	    // (device data, so the launch replays under CUDA graph capture); the
383	    // cache-pack kernel traps on a slot outside the paged window. The
384	    // every-step host guard is the caller's position bound (`decode_step`
385	    // prologue: position < max_model_len and each row confined to its
386	    // own slot region by construction).
387	
388	    // ---- absorb: ql_nope[T,heads,512] = q_pass @ W_UK ----
389	    // cuBLAS batches over this instance's heads (the full 64 or an
390	    // attention-TP shard); the T rows ride the GEMM's n dimension — column t
391	    // of head h reads q_full[t, h, 0..192] (ldb = the compact [T,heads,256]
392	    // token stride) and writes ql_nope[t, h, 0..512] (ldc = the compact
393	    // [T,heads,512] token stride).
394	    gemm_strided_batched_bf16(
395	        ctx,
396	        false,
397	        false,
398	        KV_LORA,
399	        t,
400	        QK_NOPE,
401	        &w.w_uk,
402	        KV_LORA,
403	        QK_NOPE * KV_LORA,
404	        &front.q_full,
405	        heads * Q_HEAD,
406	        Q_HEAD,
407	        &mut s.ql_nope,
408	        heads * KV_LORA,
409	        KV_LORA,
410	        heads,
411	    )?;
412	
413	    let (latent, latent_token_stride) = match (&sched.backend, &mut s.backend) {
414	        (
415	            schedule @ Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashMla { .. },
416	            Glm52MlaBackendScratch::Fp8Ds(scratch),
417	        ) => {
418	            glm52_mla_query_assemble_launch(
419	                ctx,
420	                t,
421	                heads,
422	                &s.ql_nope,
423	                &front.q_full,
424	                QK_NOPE,
425	                Q_HEAD,
426	                cos,
427	                sin,
428	                &mut scratch.query,
429	            )?;
430	            // UE8M0 scales: the FlashMLA fp8_ds_mla cache contract — the sm100
431	            // kernel truncates stored scales to powers of two (see the quant
432	            // kernel's comment); amax/448 scales silently lose up to 1 bit of
433	            // V/K magnitude per group on GB300.
434	            glm52_fp8_per_token_group_quant_bf16_ue8m0_launch(
435	                ctx,
436	                Glm52MoeQuantShape {
437	                    rows: t,
438	                    width: KV_LORA,
439	                    group_size: FP8_BLOCK,
440	                },
441	                &front.kv_c,
442	                &mut scratch.ckv_fp8,
443	                &mut scratch.ckv_scales,
444	            )?;
445	            glm52_mla_cache_pack_launch(
446	                ctx,
447	                t,
448	                &scratch.ckv_fp8,
449	                &scratch.ckv_scales,
450	                &front.k_pe,
451	                cos,
452	                sin,
453	                cache,
454	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes,
455	                contract.kv_block_stride_bytes,
456	                contract.num_blocks,
457	                slot_mapping,
458	            )?;
459	            match (schedule, &mut scratch.attend) {
460	                (
461	                    Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashMla {
462	                        tile_scheduler_metadata,
463	                        num_splits,
464	                    },
465	                    Glm52Fp8DsAttendScratch::FlashMla {
466	                        lse,
467	                        lse_accum,
468	                        o_accum,
469	                    },
470	                ) => glm52_flashmla_sparse_decode_launch(
471	                    ctx,
472	                    contract,
473	                    &scratch.query,
474	                    cache,
475	                    topk,
476	                    tile_scheduler_metadata,
477	                    num_splits,
478	                    &mut scratch.latent,
479	                    lse,
480	                    lse_accum,
481	                    o_accum,
482	                )?,
483	                _ => anyhow::bail!("GLM5.2 FP8-DS MLA schedule/scratch backend mismatch"),
484	            }
485	            (&scratch.latent, HEADS * KV_LORA)
486	        }
487	        (Glm52MlaBackendSchedule::FlashInfer, Glm52MlaBackendScratch::FlashInfer(scratch)) => {
488	            // The FlashInfer pack/attend launches address the cache dense
489	            // from its base — this backend's cache never rides a strided
490	            // slab layout.
491	            ensure!(
492	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes == 0,
493	                "GLM5.2 FlashInfer sparse decode requires a dense cache (layer offset {})",
494	                contract.kv_layer_offset_bytes
495	            );
496	            // One fused launch: query assemble + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack
497	            // (the split/norm were skipped in `glm52_mla_front_rest_into` for
498	            // this backend — the raw kv_a output is consumed directly).
499	            glm52_mla_front_pack_fp8_launch(
500	                ctx,
501	                t,
502	                heads,
503	                &s.ql_nope,
504	                &front.q_full,
505	                QK_NOPE,
506	                Q_HEAD,
507	                &front.ckv,
508	                &w.kv_a_ln.data,
509	                RMS_EPS,
510	                cos,
511	                sin,
512	                &mut scratch.query,
513	                cache,
514	                slot_mapping,
515	            )?;
516	            glm52_flashinfer_sparse_mla_fp8_launch(
517	                ctx,
518	                Glm52FlashInferSparseDecode {

72	/// UE8M0-scale (next power of two) per-token-group quant — the FlashMLA V3.2
73	/// fp8 sparse KV-cache contract. The sm100 decode kernel truncates the stored
74	/// f32 scales to e8m0 (round-toward-zero) for its block-scaled MMA, so a
75	/// non-power-of-two scale is read up to 2x too small on Blackwell; sm90 reads
76	/// f32 scales exactly. Power-of-two scales are exact on both. Use this for
77	/// every write into the 656-byte fp8_ds_mla cache and nowhere else (the MoE
78	/// and dense GEMM activations keep amax/448 scales).

80	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
81	    shape: Glm52MoeQuantShape,
82	    input: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
83	    output: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
84	    scales: &mut CudaSlice<f32>,
85	) -> Result<()> {
86	    validate_quant_buffers(shape, input, output, scales)?;
87	    let (input_ptr, _input_guard) = input.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);

# FlashMLA sm100 truncates fp8 KV-cache scales to powers of two (UE8M0)

**TL;DR**: The FlashMLA V3.2 fp8 sparse decode kernel on Blackwell (sm100/sm103, `sm100::decode::head64`) converts the 4 per-token f32 K/V scales to e8m0 with **round-toward-zero** for its tcgen05 block-scaled MMA — any non-power-of-two scale is silently read up to 2× too small. The cache **writer** must round group scales UP to the next power of two (upstream `tests/quant.py::_cast_scale_inv_to_ue8m0`); then the truncation is lossless. The sm90 kernel reads f32 scales exactly, so H200 masks the bug completely.

## How it bit us (2026-07, GLM5.2 EP4 bring-up on GB300)

- Symptom: attention output ≈ **0.67× the HF oracle at every position** (corr 0.996 — a near-pure scalar shrink), which at the decoder-layer level looks like the layer delta scaled by 0.7 early (attention-dominated) rising to ~0.95 late (MLP-dominated). The EP4 MoE oracle gate failed 23/64 probes; the failure had *nothing to do with the MoE chain*.
- Why nobody saw it earlier: EP8 runs on H200 (sm90 reads f32 scales exactly); TP4 on GB300 uses the FlashInfer backend (heads=16, 576-byte static-e4m3 cache — different format entirely). The heads=64 FlashMLA fp8-DS path had never been accuracy-gated on Blackwell. The dense layer-0 gate *was* failing on GB300 (63/64 with 0 allowed), but the smaller layer-0 delta kept the bias just under the tolerance radar.
- Diagnosis path that worked: layer gate → per-row α-fit against the oracle (engine delta = α·oracle delta) → MLA-only gate (same α at position 0 where softmax ≡ 1 ⇒ V-path, not softmax) → **weights-free kernel gate** (`pegainfer-kernels/tests/glm52_sparse_mla.rs::flashmla_sparse_vs_reference_gate`, FlashMLA vs f64 naive reference on synthetic data): single-key case off by 34%, per-128-group ratios constant (0.55/0.54/0.67/0.95) ⇒ wrong scales ⇒ implied scales all exact powers of two ⇒ read the upstream kernel: `__nv_cvt_float2_to_e8m0x2(..., cudaRoundZero)`.

## The rules

1. **Every writer of the 656-byte fp8_ds_mla cache must produce power-of-two group scales**, rounded UP (`2^ceil(log2(amax/448))`). In GLM5.2 that is the UE8M0 per-token-group quant (`glm52_fp8_per_token_group_quant_bf16_ue8m0_*`) feeding `glm52_mla_cache_pack`. Exact bit trick, no `log2f` rounding hazard: `(bits + 0x007FFFFF) & 0x7F800000`.
2. GEMM **activation** quant (MoE/dense DeepGEMM paths) keeps amax/448 scales — the contract is only about the FlashMLA KV cache.
3. Accuracy harnesses must model the cache with the same pow2 quant (`quant_dequant_groups_ue8m0` in `tools/accuracy/glm52_oracle.py`, exact via `torch.frexp`).
4. **Kimi-K2 uses the same FlashMLA sparse kernels.** It currently runs 8×H200 only; if it ever moves to Blackwell, its cache writer needs the same audit *first*.
5. When bringing up a new arch, run the weights-free kernel gate before any model-level gate — it separates "kernel/glue broken on this arch" from modeling questions in minutes.

The cache **writer** must round group scales UP to the next power of two (upstream `tests/quant.py::_cast_scale_inv_to_ue8m0`); then the truncation is lossless. The sm90 kernel reads f32 scales exactly, so H200 masks the bug completely.
4	
5	## How it bit us (2026-07, GLM5.2 EP4 bring-up on GB300)
6	
7	- Symptom: attention output ≈ **0.67× the HF oracle at every position** (corr 0.996 — a near-pure scalar shrink), which at the decoder-layer level looks like the layer delta scaled by 0.7 early (attention-dominated) rising to ~0.95 late (MLP-dominated). The EP4 MoE oracle gate failed 23/64 probes; the failure had *nothing to do with the MoE chain*.
8	- Why nobody saw it earlier: EP8 runs on H200 (sm90 reads f32 scales exactly); TP4 on GB300 uses the FlashInfer backend (heads=16, 576-byte static-e4m3 cache — different format entirely). The heads=64 FlashMLA fp8-DS path had never been accuracy-gated on Blackwell. The dense layer-0 gate *was* failing on GB300 (63/64 with 0 allowed), but the smaller layer-0 delta kept the bias just under the tolerance radar.
9	- Diagnosis path that worked: layer gate → per-row α-fit against the oracle (engine delta = α·oracle delta) → MLA-only gate (same α at position 0 where softmax ≡ 1 ⇒ V-path, not softmax) → **weights-free kernel gate** (`pegainfer-kernels/tests/glm52_sparse_mla.rs::flashmla_sparse_vs_reference_gate`, FlashMLA vs f64 naive reference on synthetic data): single-key case off by 34%, per-128-group ratios constant (0.55/0.54/0.67/0.95) ⇒ wrong scales ⇒ implied scales all exact powers of two ⇒ read the upstream kernel: `__nv_cvt_float2_to_e8m0x2(..., cudaRoundZero)`.
10	
11	## The rules
12	
13	1. **Every writer of the 656-byte fp8_ds_mla cache must produce power-of-two group scales**, rounded UP (`2^ceil(log2(amax/448))`). In GLM5.2 that is the UE8M0 per-token-group quant (`glm52_fp8_per_token_group_quant_bf16_ue8m0_*`) feeding `glm52_mla_cache_pack`. Exact bit trick, no `log2f` rounding hazard: `(bits + 0x007FFFFF) & 0x7F800000`.
14	2. GEMM **activation** quant (MoE/dense DeepGEMM paths) keeps amax/448 scales — the contract is only about the FlashMLA KV cache.
15	3. Accuracy harnesses must model the cache with the same pow2 quant (`quant_dequant_groups_ue8m0` in `tools/accuracy/glm52_oracle.py`, exact via `torch.frexp`).
16	4. **Kimi-K2 uses the same FlashMLA sparse kernels.** It currently runs 8×H200 only; if it ever moves to Blackwell, its cache writer needs the same audit *first*.
17	5. When bringing up a new arch, run the weights-free kernel gate before any model-level gate — it separates "kernel/glue broken on this arch" from modeling questions in minutes.

Let me now think about the math for the absorb section.

MLA 原理（absorbed decoding）：
- 标准注意力：每个头 h 计算 q_h · k_h^T，其中 k_h = W_UK_h @ c_kv（nope 部分）拼接 rope 部分 k_pe。
- 每头 q 的 nope 部分是 192 维：q_nope[t,h] ∈ R^192。
- k 的 nope 部分 = W_UK_h (192×512) @ c_kv (512维)。
- 点积 q_nope^T @ (W_UK_h @ c_kv) = (W_UK_h^T @ q_nope)^T @ c_kv —— 矩阵结合律：先把 q "吸收" 到 W_UK 中：q_absorbed = W_UK_h^T @ q_nope ∈ R^512。
- 这就是"weight absorption"：与其为每个缓存 token 展开 k_nope = W_UK @ c（需要缓存 192 维/头），不如缓存 512 维的 c（与头数无关）并在查询侧吸收 W_UK。
- 同样 v_h = W_UV_h @ c_kv (256×512 @ 512)，注意力输出 o_h = softmax(...) @ v = W_UV_h @ (softmax @ c_kv)。所以对 value 也可以先在 latent 空间做注意力得到 latent 输出 u_h ∈ R^512，再乘 W_UV_h 得到 v_h ∈ R^256。
- FlashMLA 的 query 维度是 512 (latent) + 64 (rope) = 576：QUERY_DIM = KV_LORA + ROPE_DIM。kernel 常量 GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_QK_HEAD_DIM=576, V_HEAD_DIM=512 (kernel 输出 latent 512 per head)。注意 kernel 侧的 "V_HEAD_DIM" = 512 是 latent 输出维度，不是模型 config 的 V_HEAD=256。

缓存收益：逐头 MHA 每层每 token 需缓存 K,V 各 64 头 × 192/256 维 ≈ 64*(192+256) = 28,672 bf16 ≈ 57,344 B；MLA 只缓存 512+64=576 个值（u4-l1 讲过 576 bf16 = 1152B 的 bf16 形式，或 fp8 cache 656B）。压缩比 28672/576 ≈ 49.8 (元素比)。

计算流程（mla_decode.rs L388-569）：
1. absorb: ql_nope[T,heads,512] = q_full[T,heads,256 的 nope 前 192] @ W_UK[heads,192,512]（batched GEMM over heads）
2. backend 分支：
   - FlashMLA: query_assemble 把 ql_nope 与 q_rope（q_full 中的 rope 部分应用 cos/sin）拼装成 [T,64,576]；UE8M0 量化 kv_c → ckv_fp8+scales；cache_pack 把 ckv_fp8、scales、rope 后的 k_pe 写入页缓存 slot_mapping[row]；flashmla_sparse_decode_launch 读 cache + topk → latent[T,64,512]
   - FlashInfer: 一个融合 launch glm52_mla_front_pack_fp8 完成查询拼装 + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack（因此 front_rest 跳过 split/norm，直接喂 raw ckv）；flashinfer_sparse_mla_fp8_launch → latent[T,16,512]
3. back: v[T,heads,256] = latent[T,heads,512] @ W_UV[heads,256,512]^T（转置 GEMM）；o_proj: v[T, heads*256] @ o_proj[6144, 16384] → o[T,6144]（fp8 GEMV 或 wide GEMM）

W_UK/W_UV 的来源：dequant_kv_b (mla_front.rs L251-298) — kv_b 原始 [heads*448, 512]，每头 448 行 = 192 (UK) + 256 (UV)；fp8 e4m3 逐 128×128 块 scale 反量化为 bf16，host 端完成（from_device 路径先 D2H 拉回再算），只在构建期做一次，运行时不再驻留 kv_b 的 fp8 形式。

后端选择 (L82-88): heads==16 且 flashinfer supported → FlashInferFp8；否则 FlashMlaFp8Ds。heads==16 出现在 TP4（64/4=16）。回退关系：FlashInfer 只支持 16 头（validate L40-44: heads==16），需要 7 个 SM100 家族 cubin；FlashMLA 走 sm_100f 组装，支持 1..=64 头（capacity 128 batch）。
- cache 格式差异: FlashMLA = 656 B/token (fp8_ds_mla: 512 fp8 + 4×f32 scales + 64 rope... 让我算一下: 512B fp8 latent + 512/128=4 groups × 4B f32 scale = 16B + rope 64 × bf16 = 128B → 512+16+128 = 656 ✓)；FlashInfer = 576 B/token (static e4m3: 512 fp8 + 64 rope fp8? 512+64=576 ✓ 标准 e4m3 无 per-group scale)。

sched metadata (L255-341):
- Glm52FlashMlaSparseDecode contract: batch_size, num_blocks, kv_layer_offset_bytes, kv_block_stride_bytes, topk, num_sm_parts, sm_scale

- folds_kv_pack: FlashInfer 后端时 front 的 split/norm 折叠进 attend 侧融合 kernel

cache-pack/query-assemble 编排 (L413-535):
- FlashMla 分支顺序: query_assemble → UE8M0 quant → cache_pack → flashmla launch
- slot_mapping 是设备数据 → CUDA graph 重放安全
- FlashInfer 分支: ensure dense cache (kv_layer_offset_bytes==0) → front_pack_fp8 融合 → flashinfer launch（贪心分解为 [8,4,2,1] 批次）

MLA 原理（absorbed decoding）：
- 标准注意力：每个头 h 计算 q_h · k_h^T，其中 k_h = W_UK_h @ c_kv（nope 部分）拼接 rope 部分 k_pe。
- 每头 q 的 nope 部分是 192 维：q_nope[t,h] ∈ R^192。
- k 的 nope 部分 = W_UK_h (192×512) @ c_kv (512维)。
- 点积 q_nope^T @ (W_UK_h @ c_kv) = (W_UK_h^T @ q_nope)^T @ c_kv —— 矩阵结合律：先把 q "吸收" 到 W_UK 中：q_absorbed = W_UK_h^T @ q_nope ∈ R^512。
- 这就是"weight absorption"：与其为每个缓存 token 展开 k_nope = W_UK @ c（需要缓存 192 维/头），不如缓存 512 维的 c（与头数无关）并在查询侧吸收 W_UK。
- 同样 v_h = W_UV_h @ c_kv (256×512 @ 512)，注意力输出 o_h = softmax(...) @ v = W_UV_h @ (softmax @ c_kv)。所以对 value 也可以先在 latent 空间做注意力得到 latent 输出 u_h ∈ R^512，再乘 W_UV_h 得到 v_h ∈ R^256。
- FlashMLA 的 query 维度是 512 (latent) + 64 (rope) = 576：QUERY_DIM = KV_LORA + ROPE_DIM。kernel 常量 GLM52_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_QK_HEAD_DIM=576, V_HEAD_DIM=512 (kernel 输出 latent 512 per head)。注意 kernel 侧的 "V_HEAD_DIM" = 512 是 latent 输出维度，不是模型 config 的 V_HEAD=256。

缓存收益：逐头 MHA 每层每 token 需缓存 K,V 各 64 头 × 192/256 维 ≈ 64*(192+256) = 28,672 bf16 ≈ 57,344 B；MLA 只缓存 512+64=576 个值（u4-l1 讲过 576 bf16 = 1152B 的 bf16 形式，或 fp8 cache 656B）。压缩比 28672/576 ≈ 49.8 (元素比)。

# u4-l3 MLA 解码后半：absorb、稀疏后端与 o_proj

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **解释吸收式解码（weight absorption）**：为什么 GLM5.2 解码时可以用「低秩 latent 注意力」替代逐头 KV——把 \(W_{UK}\) 折进查询、把 \(W_{UV}\) 留在输出侧，注意力核直接在 576 维 latent 空间里算。
2. **复述双后端的选择条件与回退关系**：`heads == 16` 且 cubin 可用走 FlashInfer fp8（576 B/token 静态 e4m3 cache），否则一律回退 FlashMLA fp8-ds（656 B/token 逐组 scale cache）。
3. **读懂 `Glm52MlaSchedMetadata`**：为什么 tile-scheduler 计划可以构建期算一次、为什么 `num_blocks` 是后绑定的占位值、`folds_kv_pack` 如何把 front 的 norm/split 折进 attend 侧。
4. **讲出 UE8M0 约束的教训来源**：FlashMLA sm100 kernel 把 f32 scale 截断成 2 的幂，GB300 上一次「输出整体缩小到 0.67×」的线上精度事故是怎么被定位、又怎么用「写入方向上取整到 2 的幂」修掉的。

本讲是 u4-l1（MLA 前半：q_a/kv_a/q_b 投影）的直接续篇：前半场把 `hidden[T, 6144]` 变成 `q_full[T, heads, 256]` 与 `ckv[T, 576]`，本讲的 `glm52_mla_attend_into` 接过这两样东西，输出注意力结果 `o[T, 6144]`。

## 2. 前置知识

- **低秩分解与结合律**：矩阵乘法满足结合律 \((AB)c = A(Bc)\)。MLA 的 K/V 不是直接算出来的，而是「压缩向量 × 上投影矩阵」：\(k_{nope,h} = W_{UK,h}\,c_{kv}\)。于是点积可以先在查询侧「吸收」权重：\(q^\top k = (W_{UK,h}^\top q)^\top c_{kv}\)。这一步换掉了「为每个缓存 token 展开逐头 K/V」的需求。
- **e4m3 与逐组 scale（回顾 u3-l1）**：fp8 e4m3 只有 8 位；GLM5.2 的投影权重按 \(128\times128\) 块携带 f32 逆 scale。KV cache 里 latent 512 维按 4 组 × 128 量化，每组一个 f32 scale。
- **UE8M0**：一种只有指数位、尾数位全零的 8 位浮点格式，即「2 的幂」。\(2^e\) 形式的数被 e8m0 截断（round-toward-zero）是无损的；非 2 的幂会被截到不大于它的 2 的幂——这正是本讲 4.3 节事故的数学根源。
- **KV 页布局（u4-l2）**：KV 活在 rank 级页池，一页 64 token；MLA 每层每 token 占一个 656 B 切片（fp8_ds_mla 格式），`kv_layer_offset_bytes` 是某层切片在页内的字节偏移，`kv_block_stride_bytes`（= 页距 3,503,040 B）是相邻页的距离。本讲的 attend launch 就靠这两个数在页池里寻址。
- **decode bucket（u1-l3/u6 预告）**：整步前向按离散行数（`[1,2,4,8,16,32,48,64,96]`）分别捕获 CUDA Graph，每个 bucket 拥有自己的 sched/scratch/graph。本讲的 sched metadata 是 per-bucket 的。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 吸收因子与 QUERY_DIM=576

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

先回忆 u4-l1 的前半场产出：每 token 每层得到

- `q_full[T, heads, 256]`：每头查询，前 192 维是 nope 部分（要和 \(W_{UK}\) 作用），后 64 维是 rope 部分；
- `kv_c[T, 512]`：latent 压缩 KV（已做 kv_a RMSNorm），**与头数无关**；
- `k_pe[T, 64]`：rope 键分量。

标准多头注意力里，每个缓存 token 每层要存「64 头 × (K 192 + V 256)」的展开量。MLA 的洞见是：K/V 展开是线性的，注意力分数和输出可以改写到 latent 空间——

\[
\text{score}(q_h, k_h) = q_{nope,h}^\top \underbrace{(W_{UK,h}\,c_{kv})}_{k_{nope,h}} + q_{rope,h}^\top k_{pe}
= \underbrace{(W_{UK,h}^\top q_{nope,h})^\top}_{\text{吸收进查询}} c_{kv} + q_{rope,h}^\top k_{pe}
\]

于是注意力核的「查询」变成 576 维：\(512\)（latent，吸收了 \(W_{UK}\)）+ \(64\)（rope）。同理 value 侧：

\[
o_h = \sum_i \alpha_i\, \underbrace{(W_{UV,h}\,c_i)}_{v_{i,h}} = W_{UV,h}\underbrace{\Big(\sum_i \alpha_i\,c_i\Big)}_{\text{latent 输出 } u_h}
\]

注意力核先输出 latent 结果 \(u_h \in \mathbb{R}^{512}\)，再由一次小 GEMM 乘 \(W_{UV,h}\) 还原成 256 维的 \(v_h\)。**代价**是查询侧两个 batched GEMM；**收益**是 cache 里每 token 只存 576 个 latent 元素而非 64×448 个展开元素。

这就是 `mla_decode.rs` 顶部注释说的 "kv_b is pre-dequantized into the bf16 absorb factors W_UK / W_UV at construction"：checkpoint 的 `kv_b_proj` 是 fp8 的 \([\,heads\times448,\,512\,]\)（每头 192 行给 UK、256 行给 UV），加载期在 host 一次性反量化成 bf16 的 `w_uk [heads,192,512]` 与 `w_uv [heads,256,512]`，运行期不再有 kv_b 的 fp8 形式。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

attend 半场对一层一批 T 行的执行序列（FlashMLA 后端视角）：

```text
q_full[T,heads,256], kv_c[T,512], k_pe[T,64]
        │
        ▼ ① 吸收 GEMM（batched over heads）
ql_nope[T,heads,512] = q_full 的 nope 192 维 @ W_UK[heads,192,512]
        │
        ▼ ② query assemble：拼 ql_nope + rope(q_rope) → query[T,64,576]
        ▼ ③ kv_c 逐组 UE8M0 量化 → ckv_fp8[T,512] + scales[T,4]
        ▼ ④ cache pack：ckv_fp8|scales|rope(k_pe) 写进 slot_mapping[row] 的页槽
        ▼ ⑤ FlashMLA 稀疏解码：按 topk 全局槽位读 cache → latent[T,64,512]
        │
        ▼ ⑥ 还原 GEMM：v[T,heads,256] = latent @ W_UV[heads,256,512]
        ▼ ⑦ o_proj：v[T, heads*256] @ o_proj → o[T,6144]
```

缓存收益的量化（每 token 每层）：

- 逐头 MHA（bf16）：\(64 \times (192+64+256) \times 2\,\text{B} = 65{,}536\,\text{B}\)；
- MLA fp8_ds cache：\(656\,\text{B}\)（构成见 4.3 节）——约 **100×** 压缩；
- 即便按 bf16 存 latent（\(576\times2=1152\,\text{B}\)）也有约 57×。

这就是 GLM5.2 能在单卡 96 行并发下把长上下文 KV 塞进显存的根本原因。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**吸收因子的出生地**——[src/mla_front.rs:251-298](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_front.rs#L251-L298)：`dequant_kv_b` 在 host 上按 128×128 块 scale 反量化 kv_b 的每个元素，行号 `r < 192` 进 `w_uk`，否则进 `w_uv`，两个 bf16 向量各上传一次设备。关键片段：

```rust
let s = scale[(row / FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols + j / FP8_BLOCK];
let val = bf16::from_f32(e4m3_to_f32(kv_b.weight[row * KV_LORA + j]) * s);
if r < QK_NOPE {
    w_uk[(h * QK_NOPE + r) * KV_LORA + j] = val;   // 192 行 → UK
} else {
    w_uv[(h * V_HEAD + (r - QK_NOPE)) * KV_LORA + j] = val; // 256 行 → UV
}
```

**生产加载路径**（不走 `from_host` 而走 `from_device`）——[src/mla_front.rs:170-181](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_front.rs#L170-L181)：已驻留的 kv_b fp8 字节先 `clone_dtoh` 拉回 host 做块 scale 反量化，随后原始 fp8 字节即被丢弃（注释明确 "it is not stored"）。启动期一次性成本，换来运行期 bf16 吸收 GEMM 不用查 scale。

**局部常量与 QUERY_DIM**——[src/mla_decode.rs:58-65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L58-L65)：模块把 config 常量起短名，最后一行就是本模块标题里的那个数：

```rust

```

注意一个命名陷阱：**kernel 侧的同名常量语义不同**。[flashmla_sparse.rs:14-15](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/flashmla_sparse.rs#L14-L15) 里 `QK_HEAD_DIM = 576`、`V_HEAD_DIM = 512`——都在 **absorbed/latent 空间**；而 config 侧 `GLM52_QK_HEAD_DIM = 256`、`GLM52_V_HEAD_DIM = 256` 在**模型空间**。读源码时先问自己「这个维度在哪个空间」。

**吸收 GEMM**——[src/mla_decode.rs:388-411](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L388-L411)：`gemm_strided_batched_bf16` 以 `heads` 为批次数，每批算 \(\text{ql\_nope}[t,h] = W_{UK,h}^{512\times192}\) 乘 `q_full` 的 nope 列块。注释里讲清了 cuBLAS 的转置技巧：T 行 ride 在 GEMM 的 n 维上，列 t 读 `q_full[t, h, 0..192]`（ldb = 紧凑的 `[T,heads,256]` token 步长）。

**还原 GEMM 与 o_proj**——[src/mla_decode.rs:537-569](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L537-L569)：第二个 batched GEMM 把 latent（FlashMLA 时全宽 `[T,64,512]`，token 步长 `HEADS*KV_LORA`）乘 \(W_{UV,h}\) 得 `v[T,heads,256]`；随后 o_proj 走 u3-l1 的 fp8 投影：行数 ≤ `FP8_GEMV_MAX_ROWS`(=8) 用 weight-only GEMV，超过则切换 `fp8_linear_large_m_into` 的 wide GEMM 路径（宽 bucket，#812 引入）：

```rust

    return crate::fp8::fp8_linear_large_m_into(ctx, &w.o_proj, t, &s.v, wide, out.data_mut());
```

#### 4.1.4 代码实践（源码阅读 + 手算）

**实践目标**：亲手验证两个 cache 格式的字节构成，确认吸收换来的压缩比。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开 [flashmla_sparse.rs:16-18](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/flashmla_sparse.rs#L16-L18) 与 [flashinfer_sparse.rs:15-16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/flashinfer_sparse.rs#L15-L16)，抄下两个 `BYTES_PER_TOKEN`。
2. 纸笔推导 656 B：512 个 e4m3 latent 字节 + \(512/128 = 4\) 组 × 4 B f32 scale + 64 个 rope 元素 × 2 B（bf16）。
3. 推导 576 B：512 个 e4m3 latent 字节 + 64 个 rope 元素 × 1 B（e4m3，静态 scale，无逐组 f32——对应 bringup 文档的 "576-byte standard E4M3"）。
4. 对照 [mla_decode.rs:166-167](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L166-L167) 的 scratch 尺寸（`ckv_fp8: t * KV_LORA` 个 u8、`ckv_scales: t * (KV_LORA / FP8_BLOCK)` 个 f32）核对你的第 2 步。
5. 计算压缩比：逐头 MHA \(64\times(192+64+256)\times2 = 65{,}536\) B 对 656 B。

**需要观察的现象**：`ckv_scales` 的长度恰是每 token 4 个 f32——这 16 B 正是 656 与 640（512+128×bf16 rope 的朴素差）之间的差值来源，也是 4.3 节 UE8M0 事故的主角。

**预期结果**：两个格式字节账都能闭合（656 / 576），压缩比 ≈ 99.9×。本实践纯纸笔 + 源码，无需 GPU。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `w_uk`/`w_uv` 用 bf16 而不是留在 fp8、在 kernel 里现查 scale？

**答案**：吸收 GEMM 是每步每层都跑的常规 batched GEMM（cuBLAS bf16）；若权重留 fp8 就需要块 scale 感知的自定义 GEMM。反量化在加载期一次完成（[mla_front.rs:255-258](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_front.rs#L255-L258)），把每步的解scale 成本变成零；且 kv_b 只在注意力里用这一种方式消费，驻留 bf16 即可。

**练习 2**：FlashMLA 输出的 `latent` 是 `[T, 64, 512]` 全宽，哪怕权重只带 16 头的 TP shard。为什么？

**答案**：FlashMLA kernel 按 64 头编译（[flashmla_sparse.rs:13](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/flashmla_sparse.rs#L13) `SPARSE_HEADS=64`），scratch 也按全宽分配（[mla_decode.rs:159](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L159)）；后续 W_UV 的 batched GEMM 只取本 shard 的头槽位（[mla_decode.rs:538-540](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L538-L540) 注释 "the batch count reads only the shard's head slots"）。

**练习 3**：把 `QUERY_DIM` 里的两个加数说清楚——各来自哪条链、谁做了 norm？

**答案**：512 = `kv_c`（kv_a 输出的压缩 KV，**经过** kv_a RMSNorm）；64 = rope 维（k_pe，**不做** norm，u4-l1 讲过的分工）。查询侧的 512 是 \(W_{UK,h}^\top q_{nope,h}\)（q 侧 norm 发生在更早的 q_a RMSNorm），rope 64 直接拼在后面。

### 4.2 双后端与 sched metadata

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

「稀疏 MLA 解码」这一步有两套可用的 kernel 栈，对应两种 cache 线格式：

| | FlashMLA fp8-ds | FlashInfer fp8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 枚举值 | `FlashMlaFp8Ds` | `FlashInferFp8` |
| 头数要求 | 1..=64（kernel 按 64 头编译） | **恰好 16**（cubin 只编译了 16 头） |
| cache 格式 | 656 B/token，逐 128 组 f32 scale（**必须 UE8M0**） | 576 B/token，静态 e4m3 无逐组 scale |
| 缓存寻址 | 支持页池 strided 布局（层偏移 + 页距） | 只认 dense cache（层偏移必须为 0） |
| 硬件依赖 | `sm_100f` 组装（Blackwell） | 7 个 SM100 家族 cubin（selector 闭包） |

选择逻辑极简——**16 头且 cubin 可用才走 FlashInfer，否则一律 FlashMLA 兜底**。16 头的场景恰是 TP4 拓扑：64 头被 4 rank 切成每 rank 16 头（attention-TP shard）；EP 拓扑每 rank 持全 64 头，永远走 FlashMLA。这就是「双后端」的分工：FlashInfer 是 TP4 带来的**专用加速路径**，FlashMLA 是**通用回退**。

`sched metadata` 要解决的问题：FlashMLA 是 split-KV 风格 kernel，每次 launch 前需要一份 tile-scheduler 计划（哪些 SM 处理哪些 tile、每个 batch 切成几份）。这份计划**只依赖 `batch_size`、`topk`、`num_sm_parts` 三个数**——不依赖位置、序列长度、层号。所以它在构建期对每个 decode bucket 算一次（78 层共享），而不是每层每步现算：注释给出的量级是 bs=1 时省掉 78 × ~25 µs/步。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
build_fixed (model/mod.rs)
  ├─ mla_heads = 全 64（EP）或 64/设备数（TP shard）
  ├─ mla_backend = glm52_select_mla_backend(mla_heads)
  ├─ 契约模板：num_blocks=1 占位（池容量此刻还没定，u2-l4）
  └─ 对 GLM52_DECODE_BUCKETS 每个 rows：
       Glm52MlaSchedMetadata::new_for_backend(契约{batch_size=rows}, heads, backend)
         ├─ FlashMLA: alloc tile_scheduler_metadata / num_splits
         │            └─ metadata_launch（构建期一次，之后整步图重放）
         └─ FlashInfer: 无计划需要
finish_kv (池容量已实测)
  └─ sched.set_num_blocks(pool_blocks)   ← 只重绑缓存几何，计划仍然有效
每层每步
  └─ attend 用 (sched, kv_layer_offset=本层切片偏移) 组装最终 launch 契约
```

「计划/契约不可能失配」是这里的类型设计要点：计划与契约住在同一个 `Glm52MlaSchedMetadata` 对象里，每个消费者都从同一个对象读两者。

### 4.3 cache-pack / query-assemble 编排（含 UE8M0 教训）

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`glm52_mla_attend_into` 的中段是两条互斥编排，把「查询拼装」「新 token 写入 cache」「稀疏注意力」串起来：

- **FlashMLA 分支（三段式）**：① query assemble 独立 kernel 把 `ql_nope` 与 rope 后的 `q_rope` 拼成 `[T,64,576]`；② kv_c 先做 **UE8M0 逐组量化**（不是普通 amax/448 量化！）；③ cache pack kernel 把 `fp8 latent + 16 B scale + bf16 rope k_pe` 写进 `slot_mapping[row]` 指定的页槽，然后 FlashMLA 按 DSA top-k 的**全局槽位**读回。
- **FlashInfer 分支（融合式）**：一个 `glm52_mla_front_pack_fp8_launch` 同时完成 query assemble + kv_a RMSNorm + cache pack 三件事——为此 front 半场必须**跳过** ckv split 与 norm（`folds_kv_pack()`），把 raw `ckv` 留给 attend 侧消费。

两个贯穿性设计：

1. **`slot_mapping` 是设备端数据**，写槽地址在 kernel 里读——所以整条链可以在 CUDA graph 里重放（u6-l3 的前提），注释称之为 graph 安全的输入重写。
2. **scale 契约按 cache 格式分流**：656 B cache 的逐组 f32 scale 必须是 2 的幂（UE8M0），而 MoE/dense GEMM 的激活量化继续用 amax/448——**这个契约只针对 FlashMLA KV cache**。

**UE8M0 教训的来源**（2026-07，GLM5.2 EP4 GB300 bring-up）：

- 症状：注意力输出在每个位置都 ≈ HF oracle 的 **0.67×**（相关系数 0.996——近乎纯标量缩小），MoE 门 23/64 探针失败，但故障其实与 MoE 无关。
- 根因：FlashMLA V3.2 sm100 kernel 用 `__nv_cvt_float2_to_e8m0x2(..., cudaRoundZero)` 把 f32 scale 截断成 e8m0 参与 tcgen05 块 scale MMA——非 2 的幂被静默读到最多小 2×。
- 为什么长期没暴露：EP8 跑 H200（sm90 kernel 读 f32 精确）；TP4 跑 GB300 但用 FlashInfer（576 B 格式根本没有逐组 scale）。**只有「64 头 FlashMLA + Blackwell」的组合才踩雷**——恰好是双后端矩阵里的空白格。
- 修复：写入方（`glm52_fp8_per_token_group_quant_bf16_ue8m0_launch`）把组 scale **向上**取整到下一个 2 的幂（位技巧 `(bits + 0x007FFFFF) & 0x7F800000`，无 `log2f` 舍入隐患）——向上取整后截断无损。数学上：

\[
\text{scale}_{\text{stored}} = 2^{\lceil \log_2(\text{amax}/448) \rceil} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \text{trunc}_{e8m0}(\text{scale}_{\text{stored}}) = \text{scale}_{\text{stored}}
\]

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
glm52_mla_attend_into 中段（伪代码）
match (sched.backend, scratch.backend):
  (FlashMla, Fp8Ds):
      query_assemble(ql_nope, q_full, cos, sin)         → query[T,64,576]
      ue8m0_quant(kv_c)                                  → ckv_fp8 + pow2 scales
      cache_pack(ckv_fp8, scales, rope(k_pe), cos, sin)  → cache[slot_mapping[row]]
      flashmla_decode(query, cache, topk, tile_plan)     → latent[T,64,512]
      latent_stride = HEADS * 512          # 全宽
  (FlashInfer, FlashInfer):
      ensure(layer_offset == 0)                           # dense cache
      front_pack_fp8(ql_nope, q_full, RAW ckv, kv_a_ln)   # 融合 assemble+norm+pack
      flashinfer_decode(query, cache, topk, seq_lens)     → latent[T,16,512]
      latent_stride = heads * 512           # shard 宽
back: v = latent @ W_UV ; o = o_proj(v)
```

FlashInfer 侧一个容易忽略的细节：它还需要 `seq_lens`（每行序列长度），FlashMLA 分支则完全由 `topk` 列表（-1 填充）驱动。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**整体编排**——[src/mla_decode.rs:413-535](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L413-L535)：一个 `match` 同时配对「计划里的后端」与「scratch 里的后端」，任何错配直接 `bail!`——schedule/scratch 在类型上无法交叉验证，就在运行时用穷举 match 兜住。

**FlashMLA 三段**——

- query assemble：[src/mla_decode.rs:418-429](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L418-L429)，读 `ql_nope` 与 `q_full`（rope 列块），用 `cos/sin` 施加 RoPE 后拼 576 维。
- UE8M0 量化：[src/mla_decode.rs:431-444](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L431-L444)。行内注释就是教训的浓缩版（"amax/448 scales silently lose up to 1 bit of V/K magnitude per group on GB300"），量化形状是 `rows=t, width=512, group=128`。
- cache pack + 解码 launch：[src/mla_decode.rs:445-484](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-glm52/src/mla_decode.rs#L445-L484)，pack 携带层偏移/页距/页数/slot_mapping；decode 消费构建期的 `tile_scheduler_metadata` 与 `num_splits`，split-KV 部分和落在 `o_accum`/`lse_accum`（长度推导 `batch + num_sm_parts` 份，见 [flashmla_sparse.rs:186-196](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/flashmla_sparse.rs#L186-L196)）。

**UE8M0 kernel 契约**——[../pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/moe_quant.rs:72-78](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/09a1a38f8b4938b06ee4e4f63f64fd4feed59434/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/glm52/moe_quant.rs#L72-L78)：doc 注释写死了使用边界——"Use this for every write into the 656-byte fp8_ds_mla cache and **nowhere else**"。
